No fresh index-level read was sourced after Investopedia's 7:56 AM PT crawl (Nasdaq -1.3%, S&P -0.4%, Dow -0.4%), so the honest read is: the morning's shape is intact, but single-stock drift points to stabilization, not acceleration. Signal: the market is still grading AI spenders on cash conversion — Alphabet's -$9.07B free cash flow and search miss versus Microsoft's $18.6B free cash flow — and tonight's Amazon/Intel reports are the next verdict on the same question. Noise: no new company headline landed in the last hour; the Marvell/Lumentum talks remain a single Bloomberg report and the Vance/Iran letter a reported overture, both unchanged from the 8 AM brief. Carried forward: Q3 GDP 3.4%, core PCE 3.1% y/y, ECB hold at 2.50% with Lagarde departing Feb 7, 2027, and ~84% December Fed-hike odds — strong growth plus as-expected hot inflation, no relief for rate-sensitive tech.

headlines.headline: Selloff easing at the edges into 9 AM: no fresher index read was sourced after Investopedia's mid-morning crawl (Nasdaq Composite -1.3%, S&P 500 -0.4%, Dow -0.4%, Nasdaq 100 -1.3%), but every megacap Finnhub quote improved slightly versus the 8 AM brief — Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon all off their morning lows.
headlines.why_it_matters: The tape is stabilizing rather than cascading — the open's read is holding, with the after-close reports now the next swing factor.

headlines.headline: Alphabet down 11.97% to $285.99 (Finnhub, vs -12.45% at 8 AM; prior close $324.89): Q3 revenue $127.58B vs ~$128.22B expected, EPS $2.12 vs ~$3.02 expected — the EPS shortfall partly reflecting an unrealized investment loss tied to SpaceX — search ads $63.35B vs $64.96B expected, -$9.07B free cash flow on $51.4B quarterly capex, with 2027 capex set to rise significantly. Cloud still doubled (+103% to $30.7B).
headlines.why_it_matters: The decline has stuck through the morning but is off its worst — the market is pricing the cash-burn plus ads-miss combination as a re-rating, not a premarket overreaction.

headlines.headline: Microsoft down 1.61% to $522.47 (Finnhub, vs -2.03% at 8 AM), from +1.5% premarket, despite the fiscal Q1 beat (revenue $92.3B, Azure +48%, $18.6B free cash flow despite $45.2B capex) and a CFO expectation of 49% Azure growth in Q2.
headlines.why_it_matters: The winner from last night is still red but recovering — in this tape even cash-backed beats are being pulled into the AI-spending risk-off move.

headlines.headline: Amazon down 2.71% to $247.70 (Finnhub, vs -3.46% at 8 AM) ahead of its after-close Q3 report (consensus EPS ~$1.97 per the premarket briefing); Intel also reports after the close.
headlines.why_it_matters: Amazon is being sold ahead of its own numbers on the same AI-capex question that hit Alphabet — tonight's AWS growth and spending guide are the next stock-specific test.

headlines.headline: Megacap divergence holds into 9 AM: Apple +1.46% to $348.84, Meta +2.58% to $628.28, Tesla +0.45% to $406.05, while Nvidia slips -0.69% to $213.89 — against Alphabet -12% and Microsoft still red.
headlines.why_it_matters: Not a uniform megacap selloff — the pressure is concentrated in Alphabet-led AI-spending names, while Apple and Meta are being treated as separate stories.

headlines.headline: Software and chips still sliding (carried from the morning read, no new update this hour): ServiceNow plunged about 25% after a small Q3 profit miss, Salesforce -5%+, Fortinet near -26% despite a beat on slowing product-revenue growth. SOXX -2%, memory ETF DRAM -3%+ after jumping 7% yesterday. Marvell -13% on the reported Lumentum deal talks; Lumentum +1.4%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The earnings-grading theme spans chips and software alike — beats are being sold on growth detail, and the Marvell leg is single-source, unconfirmed — treat the deal leg as fragile.

headlines.headline: Offsets intact outside tech (carried from the morning read): DoorDash +6% on the $17B Instacart deal; Caterpillar about -7% to -8% despite the Q3 beat, with guidance only maintained. Eli Lilly +more than 6%, Merck +5%, Chipotle +almost 7%, eBay +4%, Shell +2.6%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Healthcare and the DoorDash deal are cushioning the indexes — the Dow's drop is a Caterpillar story, not a broad blue-chip collapse.

headlines.headline: Macro steady into 9 AM: 10-year Treasury yield around 4.98%, unchanged from the 8 AM brief; WTI -2.2% to $100.47 on the reported Vance/Iran letter; Brent -1.9% to $109.56; gold -0.4% to $4,035; bitcoin near $80,000; December Fed-hike odds ~84% per CME FedWatch.
headlines.why_it_matters: Rates are not adding fresh pressure this morning — the selloff is an earnings story, not a rates story, with oil's pullback tied to a reported diplomatic overture, not a confirmed deal.
